summaryBox.title: Henry's Law
summaryBox.takeaway: p = K_H · x. Higher K_H indicates LOWER gas solubility. Dissolution is exothermic (ΔH < 0), so heating drives gases out.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
HENRY'S LAW THERMODYNAMICS

Gas Dissolution: Gas(g) + Solvent(l) ⇌ Solution(l)  (Δ_sol H < 0 [Exothermic])

• Temperature Effect: As T ↑ ⟹ Equilibrium shifts LEFT ⟹ Gas Solubility ↓
• K_H Temperature Trend: As T ↑ ⟹ K_H ↑ (Higher K_H means LOWER solubility!)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Henry's Law Equation**: $\mathbf{p = K_H \cdot x}$ where $p$ is partial pressure of gas, $x$ is dissolved mole fraction, and $K_H$ is Henry's Law constant.
• **Thermodynamics**: Gas dissolution involves a decrease in entropy ($\Delta S < 0$) and is **exothermic** ($\Delta H < 0$). According to Le Chatelier's principle, increasing temperature shifts equilibrium backwards, reducing gas solubility and increasing $K_H$.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.2 Practical Applications & Scuba Bends Prevention
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.2 Practical Applications & Scuba Bends Prevention
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
HENRY'S LAW APPLICATIONS

1. Soft Drinks / Soda: Sealed under high pressure to maximize CO₂ solubility.
2. Scuba Diving (Decompression Sickness / Bends):
   High deep-sea pressure dissolves N₂ in blood. Rapid ascent causes N₂ gas bubbles in capillaries.
   Prevention: Scuba tanks are diluted with Helium (11.7% He, 56.2% N₂, 32.1% O₂).
3. Altitude Sickness (Anoxia): Low pO₂ at high altitudes causes low blood oxygen saturation.
conceptBreakdown.content: • **Scuba Diving Bends**: In deep waters, high hydrostatic pressure forces large amounts of $\text{N}_2$ to dissolve in blood. Rapid ascent causes $\text{N}_2$ to bubble out of solution, causing painful and fatal capillary blockages (**Bends**). Diluting scuba tanks with **Helium** ($11.7\%$) prevents this due to Helium's low blood solubility.
